name: What if I have no plans or permits for my older house?

mainEntity.name: What if I have no plans or permits for my older house?

acceptedAnswer.text: If documentation is missing, rely on measured existing conditions, visible evidence, records available from the jurisdiction, and professional review rather than assumptions. Context: undocumented additions, enclosed patios, converted garages, and relocated utilities can affect design, cost, and permit discussions. Key factors: the home’s age, prior owners, property records, structural connections, utility routes, and whether the current layout matches available documents. Practical guidance: disclose uncertainty at the first consultation and photograph areas that may have been altered. Ask which conditions must be verified before design is finalized. A clearly labeled unknown is safer than an inaccurate plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start with measured existing conditions and disclose the missing records. Gather whatever assessor, inspection, or previous-sale documents you have, then ask the remodeling team to identify which walls, utilities, additions, and conversions need field verification before design or permit submittal.
